threat_actor.caption: Threat Actor
threat_actor.description: A threat actor is an individual or group that conducts malicious cyber activities, often with financial, political, or ideological motives.

tlp.caption: Traffic Light Protocol
tlp.description: The Traffic Light Protocol (TLP) was created to facilitate greater sharing of potentially sensitive information and more effective collaboration. TLP provides a simple and intuitive schema for indicating with whom potentially sensitive information can be shared.

AMBER.caption: TLP:AMBER
AMBER.description: TLP:AMBER is for limited disclosure, recipients can only spread this on a need-to-know basis within their organization and its clients. Note that TLP:AMBER+STRICT restricts sharing to the organization only. Sources may use TLP:AMBER when information requires support to be effectively acted upon, yet carries risk to privacy, reputation, or operations if shared outside of the organizations involved. Recipients may share TLP:AMBER information with members of their own organization and its clients, but only on a need-to-know basis to protect their organization and its clients and prevent further harm. Note: if the source wants to restrict sharing to the organization only, they must specify TLP:AMBER+STRICT.

AMBER STRICT.caption: TLP:AMBER+STRICT
AMBER STRICT.description: TLP:AMBER is for limited disclosure, recipients can only spread this on a need-to-know basis within their organization and its clients. Note that TLP:AMBER+STRICT restricts sharing to the organization only. Sources may use TLP:AMBER when information requires support to be effectively acted upon, yet carries risk to privacy, reputation, or operations if shared outside of the organizations involved. Recipients may share TLP:AMBER information with members of their own organization and its clients, but only on a need-to-know basis to protect their organization and its clients and prevent further harm. Note: if the source wants to restrict sharing to the organization only, they must specify TLP:AMBER+STRICT.

CLEAR.caption: TLP:CLEAR
CLEAR.description: TLP:CLEAR denotes that recipients can spread this to the world, there is no limit on disclosure. Sources may use TLP:CLEAR when information carries minimal or no foreseeable risk of misuse, in accordance with applicable rules and procedures for public release. Subject to standard copyright rules, TLP:CLEAR information may be shared without restriction.

GREEN.caption: TLP:GREEN
GREEN.description: TLP:GREEN is for limited disclosure, recipients can spread this within their community. Sources may use TLP:GREEN when information is useful to increase awareness within their wider community. Recipients may share TLP:GREEN information with peers and partner organizations within their community, but not via publicly accessible channels. TLP:GREEN information may not be shared outside of the community. Note: when “community” is not defined, assume the cybersecurity/defense community.

RED.caption: TLP:RED
RED.description: TLP:RED is for the eyes and ears of individual recipients only, no further disclosure. Sources may use TLP:RED when information cannot be effectively acted upon without significant risk for the privacy, reputation, or operations of the organizations involved. Recipients may therefore not share TLP:RED information with anyone else. In the context of a meeting, for example, TLP:RED information is limited to those present at the meeting.

WHITE.caption: TLP:WHITE
WHITE.description: TLP:WHITE and TLP:CLEAR may be used interchangeably, TLP:WHITE is the most up to date (as of TLP 2.0) usage.

This information can be used to further enrich a detection or finding by providing decisioning support to other analysts and engineers.

purl.description: A purl is a URL string used to identify and locate a software package in a mostly universal and uniform way across programming languages, package managers, packaging conventions, tools, APIs and databases.

sequence_number.description: The relative order number of this packet within its capture context (such as a PCAP file, network session, or reconstructed stream). This represents chronological capture order, distinct from both protocol-level sequencing (such as TCP sequence numbers).

source.description: The human-readable name describing how or where the packet was obtained. This should match the caption associated with source_id. If source_id is 99 (Other), this field contains the original data source–specific value.

source_id.description: A normalized numeric identifier that specifies how the packet was obtained or generated.

2.caption: Stream

3.caption: Decoder
3.description: The packet was generated or extracted by a protocol decoder or analysis engine.

4.caption: TAP
4.description: The packet was captured from a physical network Test Access Point (TAP) device used for passive monitoring.

5.caption: SPAN
5.description: The packet was captured from a switch Switched Port Analyzer (SPAN) or mirror port.

6.caption: Endpoint
6.description: The packet was captured by a host-based agent or endpoint detection and response (EDR) sensor.

7.caption: Virtual
7.description: The packet was captured from a virtual network interface, virtual switch, or container network.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The packet source is not mapped. Refer to the source field for the original source-specific value.

start_offset.caption: Start Offset
start_offset.description: The starting byte position of this packet within a capture file or stream.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The actual packet data, represented as a string. The format of this string is determined by the specified encoding_id (e.g., Base64, Hexadecimal, or URL Encoded).

packet.description: The Packet object represents a single captured network packet and its associated metadata. It describes where the packet came from, how it is stored or encoded, and how it can be located within a capture file or stream. This object does not interpret protocol content; it only represents the captured packet data and its positioning information.

When a process hosts multiple agents and the activity cannot be attributed to one specifically, use hosted_ai_agent_list instead.

ancestry.caption: Ancestry
ancestry.description: An array of Process Entities describing the extended parentage of this process object. Direct parent information should be expressed through the parent_process attribute. The first array element is the direct parent of this process object. Subsequent list elements go up the process parentage hierarchy. That is, the array is sorted from newest to oldest process. It is recommended to only populate this field for the top-level process object.

Use when a single process hosts multiple agents (e.g., an IDE running several coding agents within the same host process) and the producer cannot attribute a specific activity to a single agent. When attribution is available, populate the singular ai_agent attribute instead.

9.caption: Probably Malicious
9.description: Indicators of maliciousness.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The reputation score is not mapped. See the rep_score attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

reputation.caption: Reputation
reputation.description: The Reputation object describes the reputation/risk score of an entity (e.g. device, user, domain).
reputation.name: reputation

containers.caption: Containers
containers.description: When working with containerized applications, the set of containers which write to the standard the output of a particular logging driver. For example, this may be the set of containers involved in handling api requests and responses for a containerized application.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The additional data that is associated with the api request.

flags.caption: Flags
flags.description: The communication flags that are associated with the api request.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique request identifier.

request.caption: Request Elements
request.description: The Request Elements object describes characteristics of an API request.
request.name: request

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

cloud_partition.caption: Cloud Partition
cloud_partition.description: The logical grouping or isolated segment within a cloud provider's infrastructure where the resource is located. Examples include AWS partitions (aws, aws-cn, aws-us-gov), Azure cloud environments (AzureCloud, AzureUSGovernment, AzureChinaCloud), or similar logical divisions in other cloud providers.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the resource was created.

criticality.caption: Criticality
criticality.description:
Criticality or relative importance of this resource, normalized to the caption of criticality_id. In the case of Other, the value is defined by the event source.

Note: For versions prior to 1.9, criticality_id was not available and this is a source specific value.

criticality_id.caption: Criticality Level ID
criticality_id.description: The normalized identifier for the criticality or relative importance of this resource. Select the value that best reflects the operational and security impact if the resource were compromised or made unavailable. See the criticality sibling attribute for the corresponding human-readable label.

1.caption: Low
1.description: Minimal operational or security importance.

2.caption: Medium
2.description: Affects localized functions or specific business processes.

3.caption: High
3.description: Critical to core operations. Compromise leads to significant, but recoverable disruptions.

4.caption: Very High
4.description: Mission critical, essential to business survival. Compromise could result in catastrophic consequences.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The criticality level is not mapped. See the criticality attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

device.caption: Device
device.description: The device details when the resource type is a device — for example, a cloud compute instance, a laptop, or a network appliance. Provides structured device attributes (OS, type, hardware, agent) that the resource's scalar fields cannot represent — beyond what the hostname and ip attributes capture. The device.name and device.uid should match the name and uid of this objects; the device.hostname value should match the hostname attribute of this object. The top-level hostname and ip remain the primary identifiers for the device resource.

group.caption: Group
group.description: The name of the related resource group.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The fully qualified name of the resource. If the resource is a device, this should match device.hostname.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address of the resource, in either IPv4 or IPv6 format. If the resource is a device, this should match device.ip.

is_backed_up.caption: Back Ups Configured
is_backed_up.description: Indicates whether the device or resource has a backup enabled, such as an automated snapshot or a cloud backup. For example, this is indicated by the cloudBackupEnabled value within JAMF Pro mobile devices or the registration of an AWS ARN with the AWS Backup service.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the resource.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the resource was last modified.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the resource.

namespace.caption: Namespace
namespace.description: The namespace is useful when similar entities exist that you need to keep separate.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The details of the entity that owns the resource. Usually not the same as user that may not own the resource. For example the owner of the directory server but not a user in the directory. This object includes properties such as the owner's name, unique identifier, type, domain, and other relevant attributes that help identify the resource owner within the environment.

provider.caption: Cloud Provider
provider.description: The cloud service provider that hosts or manages the resource. This field is typically used when the resource is managed by a different provider than the one generating the event or finding. Examples include AWS, Azure, GCP (Google Cloud Platform), Oracle Cloud, IBM Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, or other public, private, or hybrid cloud providers.

region.caption: Region
region.description: The cloud region where the resource is hosted, as defined by the cloud provider. This represents the physical or logical geographic area containing the infrastructure supporting the resource. Examples include AWS regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1), Azure regions (East US, West Europe), GCP regions (us-central1, europe-west1), or Oracle Cloud regions (us-ashburn-1, uk-london-1).

resource_relationship.caption: Resource Relationship
resource_relationship.description: A graph representation showing how this resource relates to and interacts with other entities in the environment. This can include parent/child relationships, dependencies, or other connections.

role.caption: Role
role.description: The role of the resource in the context of the event or finding, normalized to the caption of the role_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

role_id.caption: Role ID
role_id.description: The normalized identifier of the resource's role in the context of the event or finding.

1.caption: Target
1.description: The resource is the primary target or subject of the event/finding.

2.caption: Actor
2.description: The resource is acting as the initiator or performer in the context of the event/finding.

3.caption: Affected
3.description: The resource was impacted or affected by the event/finding.

4.caption: Related
4.description: The resource is related to or associated with the event/finding.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The role is not mapped. See the role attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the resource.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The resource type as defined by the event source.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the resource.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: The alternative unique identifier of the resource.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user represented by this resource — for example, a cloud IAM user, a local account, or an application identity. Provides structured user attributes (email, groups, privileges) that this object's scalar fields such as name cannot represent. Distinct from owner, which identifies the entity responsible for managing the resource. The user.name value should match the name attribute of this object, user.uid should match the uid of this object.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the resource. For example 1.2.3.

zone.caption: Cloud Availability Zone
zone.description: The availability zone within a cloud region where the resource is located. Examples include AWS availability zones (us-east-1a, us-east-1b), Azure availability zones (1, 2, 3 within a region), GCP zones (us-central1-a, us-central1-b), or Oracle Cloud availability domains (AD-1, AD-2, AD-3).

resource_details.caption: Resource Details
resource_details.description: The Resource Details object describes details about a resource (including a user) affected by or related to the activity or finding. The name and/or uid should correspond to the resource for which the details pertain. Use role_id to characterize the role of the resource.
resource_details.name: resource_details

code.caption: Response Code
code.description: The numeric response sent to a request.

containers.caption: Containers
containers.description: When working with containerized applications, the set of containers which write to the standard the output of a particular logging driver. For example, this may be the set of containers involved in handling api requests and responses for a containerized application.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The additional data that is associated with the api response.

flags.caption: Flags
flags.description: The communication flags that are associated with the api response.

message.caption: Message
message.description: The response message provided by the service or API.

response.caption: Response Elements
response.description: The Response Elements object describes characteristics of an API response.
response.name: response

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the rule that generated the event.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the rule that generated the event.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The rule type.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the rule that generated the event.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

rule.caption: Rule
rule.description: The Rule object describes characteristics of a rule associated with a policy or an event.
rule.name: rule

name.caption: Name
name.description: Name of SAN (e.g. The actual IP Address or domain.)

type.caption: Type
type.description: Type descriptor of SAN (e.g. IP Address/domain/etc.)

san.caption: Subject Alternative Name
san.description: The Subject Alternative name (SAN) object describes a SAN secured by a digital certificate
san.name: san

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the SBOM was created.

package.caption: Software Package
package.description: The software package or library that is being discovered or inventoried by an SBOM.

product.caption: Product
product.description: Details about the upstream product that generated the SBOM e.g. cdxgen or Syft.

software_components.caption: Software Components
software_components.description: The list of software components used in the software package.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of SBOM, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source.

1.caption: SPDX
1.description: System Package Data Exchange (SPDX®) is an open standard capable of representing systems with software components in as SBOMs (Software Bill of Materials) and other AI, data and security references supporting a range of risk management use cases. The SPDX specification is a freely available international open standard (ISO/IEC 5692:2021).

2.caption: CycloneDX
2.description: CycloneDX is an International Standard for Bill of Materials (ECMA-424).

3.caption: SWID
3.description: The International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) publishes, ISO/IEC 19770-2, a standard for software identification (SWID) tags that defines a structured metadata format for describing a software product. A SWID tag document is composed of a structured set of data elements that identify the software product

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: SBOM ID
uid.description: A unique identifier for the SBOM or the SBOM generation by a source tool, such as the SPDX metadata.component.bom-ref.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The specification (spec) version of the particular SBOM, e.g., 1.6.

sbom.caption: Software Bill of Materials
sbom.description: The Software Bill of Materials object describes characteristics of a generated SBOM.
sbom.name: sbom

auth_protocol.caption: Auth Protocol
auth_protocol.description: The authorization protocol as defined by the caption of auth_protocol_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

auth_protocol_id.caption: Auth Protocol ID
auth_protocol_id.description: The normalized identifier of the authorization protocol used by the SCIM resource.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The authentication protocol is not mapped. See the auth_protocol attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: When the SCIM resource was added to the service provider.

error_message.caption: Last Error Message
error_message.description: Message or code associated with the last encountered error.

is_group_provisioning_enabled.caption: SCIM Group Provisioning Enabled
is_group_provisioning_enabled.description: Indicates whether the SCIM resource is configured to provision groups, automatically or otherwise.

is_user_provisioning_enabled.caption: SCIM User Provisioning Enabled
is_user_provisioning_enabled.description: Indicates whether the SCIM resource is configured to provision users, automatically or otherwise.

last_run_time.caption: Last Sync Time
last_run_time.description: Timestamp of the most recent successful synchronization.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The most recent time when the SCIM resource was updated at the service provider.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the SCIM resource.

protocol_name.caption: Supported Protocol
protocol_name.description: The supported protocol for the SCIM resource. E.g., SAML, OIDC, or OAuth2.

rate_limit.caption: Rate Limit
rate_limit.description: Maximum number of requests allowed by the SCIM resource within a specified time frame to avoid throttling.

scim_group_schema.caption: SCIM Group Schema
scim_group_schema.description: SCIM provides a schema for representing groups, identified using the following schema URI: urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group as defined in RFC 7634. This attribute will capture key-value pairs for the scheme implemented in a SCIM resource.

scim_user_schema.caption: SCIM User Schema
scim_user_schema.description: SCIM provides a resource type for user resources. The core schema for user is identified using the following schema URI: urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User as defined in RFC 7634. This attribute will capture key-value pairs for the scheme implemented in a SCIM resource. This object is inclusive of both the basic and Enterprise User Schema Extension.

state.caption: State
state.description: The provisioning state of the SCIM resource, normalized to the caption of the state_id value. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

state_id.caption: State ID
state_id.description: The normalized state ID of the SCIM resource to reflect its activation status.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The provisioning state of the SCIM resource is unknown.

1.caption: Pending
1.description: The SCIM resource is Pending activation or creation.

2.caption: Active
2.description: The SCIM resource is in an Active state, or otherwise enabled.

3.caption: Failed
3.description: The SCIM resource is in a Failed state.

4.caption: Deleted
4.description: The SCIM resource is in a Deleted state, or otherwise disabled.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The provisioning state of the SCIM resource is not mapped. See the state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique identifier for a SCIM resource as defined by the service provider.

uid_alt.caption: External ID
uid_alt.description: A String that is an identifier for the resource as defined by the provisioning client. The externalId may simplify identification of a resource between the provisioning client and the service provider by allowing the client to use a filter to locate the resource with an identifier from the provisioning domain, obviating the need to store a local mapping between the provisioning domain's identifier of the resource and the identifier used by the service provider.

url_string.caption: SCIM Endpoint URL
url_string.description: The primary URL for SCIM API requests.

vendor_name.caption: Service Provider
vendor_name.description: Name of the vendor or service provider implementing SCIM. E.g., Okta, Auth0, Microsoft.

scim.caption: SCIM
scim.description: The System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) Configuration object provides a structured set of attributes related to SCIM protocols used for identity provisioning and management across cloud-based platforms. It standardizes user and group provisioning details, enabling identity synchronization and lifecycle management with compatible Identity Providers (IdPs) and applications. SCIM is defined in RFC 7634.
scim.name: scim

file.caption: File
file.description: Present if this script is associated with a file. Not present in the case of a file-less script.

hashes.caption: Hashes
hashes.description: An array of the script's cryptographic hashes. Note that these hashes are calculated on the script in its original encoding, and not on the normalized UTF-8 encoding found in the script_content attribute.

name.caption: Name
name.description: Unique identifier for the script or macro, independent of the containing file, used for tracking, auditing, and security analysis.

parent_uid.caption: Parent Unique ID
parent_uid.description: This attribute relates a sub-script to a parent script having the matching uid attribute. In the case of PowerShell, sub-script execution can be identified by matching the activity correlation ID of the raw ETW events provided by the OS.

script_content.caption: Script Content
script_content.description: The script content, normalized to UTF-8 encoding irrespective of its original encoding. When emitting this attribute, it may be appropriate to truncate large scripts. When consuming this attribute, large scripts should be anticipated.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The script type, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The script type is not mapped. See the type attribute which contains an event source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: Some script engines assign a unique ID to each individual execution of a given script. This attribute captures that unique ID. In the case of PowerShell, the unique ID corresponds to the ScriptBlockId in the raw ETW events provided by the OS.

script.caption: Script
script.description: The Script object describes a script or command that can be executed by a shell, script engine, or interpreter. Examples include Bash, JavsScript, PowerShell, Python, VBScript, etc. Note that the term script here denotes not only a script contained within a file but also a script or command typed interactively by a user, supplied on the command line, or provided by some other file-less mechanism.
script.name: script

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the entity.

sensor_layer.caption: Sensor Layer
sensor_layer.description: The technology or sensor layer that emitted the data, normalized to the caption of sensor_layer_id. When sensor_layer_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific label.

sensor_layer_id.caption: Sensor Layer ID
sensor_layer_id.description: The normalized identifier of the sensor layer that emitted the data. For example, use this to classify the detection surface (e.g., IPS sensor, endpoint agent, email gateway). When the type is not listed, use 99 (Other) and populate sensor_layer with the source-specific label.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The sensor layer type is Unknown.

1.caption: Network
1.description: The analyzed data is emitted by, or originates from a network, firewall, or IPS sensor.

2.caption: Endpoint
2.description: The analyzed data is emitted by, or originates from an endpoint device or agent running on an OS.

3.caption: Email
3.description: The analyzed data is emitted by, or originates from an email gateway or email security system.

4.caption: IAM
4.description: The analyzed data is emitted by, or originates from an identity and access management (IAM) system or service.

5.caption: Proxy
5.description: The analyzed data is emitted by, or originates from a proxy server (e.g., forward or reverse proxy, web gateway).

6.caption: Threat Intel
6.description: The analyzed data is emitted by, or originates from a cyber threat intelligence (CTI) system or by matching observables against a threat intelligence feed or report.

7.caption: Application
7.description: The analyzed data is emitted by, or originates from an application (e.g., web application, SaaS platform, or custom business application).

99.caption: Other
99.description: The sensor layer type is not mapped. See the sensor_layer attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.description: The unique identifier of the entity.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

sensor_info.caption: Sensor Information
sensor_info.description: The Sensor Information object describes a control point sensor that emits data, or originates detections. It can be part of an endpoint or agent running on an OS, a SaaS application, a network device, a Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) system, or other detection and enforcement technologies.

labels.caption: Labels

name.description: The name of the service.

tags.caption: Tags

credential_uid.caption: User Credential ID
credential_uid.description: The unique identifier of the user's credential. For example, AWS Access Key ID.

expiration_reason.caption: Expiration Reason
expiration_reason.description: The reason which triggered the session expiration.

is_mfa.caption: Multi Factor Authentication
is_mfa.description: Indicates whether Multi Factor Authentication was used during authentication.

is_remote.caption: Remote

uuid.description: The universally unique identifier of the session.

session.caption: Session

author.description: The author(s) who published the software component.

hash.caption: Hash

license.caption: Software License

99.caption: Other
99.description: The threat actor type is not mapped.

threat_actor.caption: Threat Actor
threat_actor.description: Threat actor is responsible for the observed malicious activity.
threat_actor.name: threat_actor

duration.caption: Duration Milliseconds
duration.description: The duration of the time span in milliseconds.

duration_days.caption: Duration Days
duration_days.description: The duration of the time span in days.

duration_hours.caption: Duration Hours
duration_hours.description: The duration of the time span in hours.

duration_mins.caption: Duration Minutes
duration_mins.description: The duration of the time span in minutes.

duration_months.caption: Duration Months
duration_months.description: The duration of the time span in months.

duration_secs.caption: Duration Seconds
duration_secs.description: The duration of the time span in seconds.

duration_weeks.caption: Duration Weeks
duration_weeks.description: The duration of the time span in weeks.

duration_years.caption: Duration Years
duration_years.description: The duration of the time span in years.

end_time.caption: End Time
end_time.description: The end time or conclusion of the timespan's interval.

start_time.caption: Start Time
start_time.description: The start time or beginning of the timespan's interval.

type.caption: Time Span Type
type.description: The type of time span duration the object represents.

type_id.caption: Time Span Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized identifier for the time span duration type.

9.caption: Time Interval
9.description: The start_time and end_time should be set.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

timespan.caption: Time Span
timespan.description:
The Time Span object represents different time period durations. If a timespan is fractional, i.e. crosses one period, e.g. a week and 3 days, more than one may be populated since each member is of integral type. In that case type_id if present should be set to Other.

A timespan may also be defined by its time interval boundaries, start_time and end_time.
timespan.name: timespan

alert.caption: Client TLS Alert
alert.description: The integer value of a TLS alert per the TLS specification.

certificate.caption: Certificate
certificate.description: The certificate object containing information about the digital certificate.

certificate_chain.caption: Certificate Chain
certificate_chain.description: The Chain of Certificate Serial Numbers field provides a chain of Certificate Issuer Serial Numbers leading to the Root Certificate Issuer.

client_ciphers.caption: Client Cipher Suites
client_ciphers.description: The client cipher suites that were exchanged during the TLS handshake negotiation.

handshake_dur.caption: Handshake Duration
handshake_dur.description: The amount of total time for the TLS handshake to complete after the TCP connection is established, including client-side delays, in milliseconds.

ja3_hash.caption: JA3 Hash
ja3_hash.description: The MD5 hash of a JA3 string.

ja3s_hash.caption: JA3S Hash
ja3s_hash.description: The MD5 hash of a JA3S string.

key_length.caption: Key Length
key_length.description: The length of the encryption key.

sans.caption: Subject Alternative Names
sans.description: The list of subject alternative names that are secured by a specific certificate.

server_ciphers.caption: Server Cipher Suites
server_ciphers.description: The server cipher suites that were exchanged during the TLS handshake negotiation.

sni.caption: Server Name Indication
sni.description: The Server Name Indication (SNI) extension sent by the client.

tls.caption: Transport Layer Security (TLS)
tls.description: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) object describes the negotiated TLS protocol used for secure communications over an establish network connection.
tls.name: tls

data.caption: Data
data.description: The data contains information specific to the particular extension type.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The TLS extension type. For example: Server Name.

1.caption: maximum_fragment_length
1.description: The Maximum Fragment Length Negotiation extension.

14.caption: use_srtp
14.description: The Use SRTP data protection extension.

45.caption: psk_key_exchange_modes
45.description: The Pre-Shared Key Exchange Modes extension.

5.caption: status_request
5.description: The Certificate Status Request extension.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

tls_extension.caption: TLS Extension
tls_extension.description: The TLS Extension object describes additional attributes that extend the base Transport Layer Security (TLS) object.
tls_extension.name: tls_extension

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time that the token was created.

expiration_time.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time.description: The expiration time of the token.

is_renewable.caption: Renewable
is_renewable.description: Indicates whether the token is renewable.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The last time the token was updated.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The human-friendly name of a token or key, if available, such as the name from the Okta API Token API.

tenant_uid.caption: Tenant UID
tenant_uid.description: The unique identifier of the tenant or organization that owns the token or key, or the tenant context in which the token is authorized for use. This is particularly relevant in multi-tenant Identity Provider scenarios where tokens are scoped to specific tenants.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the token, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. This indicates whether the token is a Client Token, API Token, or one of the protocol-specific token types.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized token type identifier. Valid values: 0 (Unknown), 1 (Ticket Granting Ticket - Kerberos), 2 (Service Ticket - Kerberos), 3 (Identity Token - OIDC), 4 (Refresh Token - OIDC), 5 (SAML Assertion), 6 (Client Token - IdP-issued), 7 (API Token - generic API keys), 99 (Other).

1.caption: Ticket Granting Ticket
1.description: Ticket Granting Ticket (TGT) for Kerberos.

2.caption: Service Ticket
2.description: Service Ticket (ST) for Kerberos.

3.caption: Identity Token
3.description: Identity (ID) Token for OIDC.

4.caption: Refresh Token
4.description: Refresh Token for OIDC.

5.caption: SAML Assertion
5.description: Authentication Assertion for SAML.

6.caption: Client Token
6.description: Client Token issued by an Identity Provider (IdP) for application authentication. Use this value for IdP-issued tokens used for service-to-service authentication. Examples: Microsoft Entra ID Application Registration client secrets, Okta API tokens, Auth0 Machine-to-Machine tokens. Key characteristic: These tokens are issued by Identity Providers, not by individual services.

7.caption: API Token
7.description: A generic API token or API key used for authenticating API requests. Use this value for service-specific API authentication tokens that are NOT issued by Identity Providers. Examples: REST API keys, GraphQL API keys, Stripe API keys, Twilio API keys, AWS API keys. Key characteristic: These tokens are issued by individual services/platforms, not by Identity Providers.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique ID of a token or key, if available, such as the Secret ID of Entra ID Application Registration Client Secrets.

zone.caption: Network Zone
zone.description: The network zone or geographic region that the token or key is authorized to be used from. This may represent network-based access restrictions, geographic limitations, or other zone-based authorization policies. Examples include Okta's network zone restrictions or cloud provider region restrictions.

token.caption: Token
token.description: The Token object is the base object for representing tokens, API keys, and authentication credentials used across different contexts. This object provides common attributes for all token types, including protocol-specific authentication tokens (Kerberos, OIDC, SAML) and API/client tokens used for service authentication. When to use this object: Use the base token object directly in API activity events to represent API tokens, client tokens, or API keys used to authenticate API requests. Examples include: Okta API tokens, Microsoft Entra ID Application Registration client secrets, Stripe API keys, AWS API keys. When NOT to use this object: Do NOT use the base token object for protocol-specific authentication tokens in authentication events - use authentication_token instead (which extends this object). Do NOT use token for tracking credential lifecycle and usage patterns - use programmatic_credential instead.
token.name: token

lang.caption: Language
lang.description: The transformation language used to transform the data.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the transformation or mapping.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product or instance used to make the transformation

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the mapping or transformation.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

url_string.caption: URL String
url_string.description: The Uniform Resource Locator String where the mapping or transformation exists.

transformation_info.caption: Transformation Info
transformation_info.description: The transformation_info object represents the mapping or transformation used.
transformation_info.name: transformation_info

algorithm.caption: Algorithm
algorithm.description: The HMAC algorithm used to compute the MAC. For example: hmac-sha256.

error.caption: TSIG Error
error.description: The TSIG error, normalized to the caption of the error_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

error_id.caption: TSIG Error ID
error_id.description: The normalized TSIG-specific error code as defined in RFC 2845 and RFC 6895. This is independent of the DNS message header RCODE.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The TSIG error code is not listed. See the error attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

key_name.caption: Key Name
key_name.description: The name of the shared secret key used to sign the DNS message. For example: my-tsig-key.example.com.

tsig.caption: TSIG
tsig.description: The TSIG (Transaction Signature) object represents a TSIG resource record as defined in RFC 2845. TSIG uses a shared secret key and one-way hash function to authenticate DNS messages. Per RFC 2845, at most one TSIG record is permitted per DNS message.
tsig.name: tsig

categories.caption: Website Categorization
categories.description: The Website categorization names, as defined by category_ids enum values.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The Domain/URL category is not mapped. See the categories attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The domain portion of the URL. For example: example.com in https://sub.example.com.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The URL host as extracted from the URL. For example: www.example.com from www.example.com/download/trouble.

path.caption: Path
path.description: The URL path as extracted from the URL. For example: /download/trouble from www.example.com/download/trouble.

query_string.caption: HTTP Query String
query_string.description: The query portion of the URL. For example: the query portion of the URL http://www.example.com/search?q=bad&sort=date is q=bad&sort=date.

resource_type.caption: Resource Type
resource_type.description: The context in which a resource was retrieved in a web request.

scheme.caption: Scheme
scheme.description: The scheme portion of the URL. For example: http, https, ftp, or sftp.

subdomain.caption: Subdomain
subdomain.description: The subdomain portion of the URL. For example: sub in https://sub.example.com or sub2.sub1 in https://sub2.sub1.example.com.

url_string.caption: URL String
url_string.description: The URL string. See RFC 1738. For example: http://www.example.com/download/trouble.exe. Note: The URL path should not populate the URL string.

url.caption: Uniform Resource Locator
url.description: The Uniform Resource Locator (URL) object describes the characteristics of a URL.
url.name: url

account.caption: Account
account.description: The user's account or the account associated with the user.

credential_uid.caption: User Credential ID
credential_uid.description: The unique identifier of the user's credential. For example, AWS Access Key ID.

display_name.caption: Display Name
display_name.description: The display name of the user, as reported by the product.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The domain where the user is defined. For example: the LDAP or Active Directory domain.

full_name.caption: Full Name
full_name.description: The full name of the user, as reported by the product.

groups.caption: Groups
groups.description: The administrative groups to which the user belongs.

has_mfa.caption: MFA Assigned
has_mfa.description: The user has a multi-factor or secondary-factor device assigned.

ldap_person.caption: LDAP Person
ldap_person.description: The additional LDAP attributes that describe a person.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The username. For example, janedoe1.

org.caption: Organization
org.description: Organization and org unit related to the user.

phone_number.caption: Telephone Number
phone_number.description: The telephone number of the user.

programmatic_credentials.caption: Programmatic Credentials
programmatic_credentials.description: Details about the programmatic credential (API keys, access tokens, certificates, etc) associated to the user.

risk_level.caption: Risk Level
risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The risk level is not mapped. See the risk_level attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the user. For example, System, AWS IAM User, etc.

1.caption: User
1.description: Regular user account.

2.caption: Admin
2.description: Admin/root user account.

3.caption: System
3.description: System account. For example, Windows computer accounts with a trailing dollar sign ($).

4.caption: Service
4.description: Service account. For example, Windows service account.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique user identifier. For example, the Windows user SID, ActiveDirectory DN or AWS user ARN.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: The alternate user identifier. For example, the Active Directory user GUID or AWS user Principal ID.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

user.caption: User
user.description: The User object describes the characteristics of a user/person or a security principal.
user.name: user

advisory.caption: Security Advisory
advisory.description: Detail about the security advisory, that is used to publicly disclose cybersecurity vulnerabilities by a vendor.

affected_code.caption: Affected Code
affected_code.description: List of Affected Code objects that describe details about code blocks identified as vulnerable.

affected_packages.caption: Affected Software Packages
affected_packages.description: List of software packages identified as affected by a vulnerability/vulnerabilities.

category.caption: Category
category.description: The category of a vulnerability or weakness, as reported by the source tool, such as Container Security or Open Source Security.

cve.caption: CVE
cve.description: Describes the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) details related to the vulnerability.

cwe.caption: CWE
cwe.description: Describes the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) details related to the vulnerability.

dependency_chain.caption: Dependency Chain
dependency_chain.description: Information about the chain of dependencies related to the issue as reported by an Application Security or Vulnerability Management tool. E.g., serverless-offline -> @serverless/utils -> memoizee -> es5-ext.

exploit_last_seen_time.caption: Exploit Last Seen Time
exploit_last_seen_time.description: The time when the exploit was most recently observed.

exploit_ref_url.caption: Exploit URL
exploit_ref_url.description: The URL of the exploit code or Proof-of-Concept (PoC).

exploit_requirement.caption: Exploit Requirement
exploit_requirement.description: The requirement description related to any constraints around exploit execution.

exploit_type.caption: Exploit Type
exploit_type.description: The categorization or type of Exploit. E.g., Network or Physical.

first_seen_time.caption: First Seen
first_seen_time.description: The time when the vulnerability was first observed.

fix_available.caption: Fix Availability
fix_available.description: Indicates if a fix is available for the reported vulnerability.

fix_coverage.caption: Fix Coverage
fix_coverage.description: The fix coverage, normalized to the caption of the fix_coverage_id value.

fix_coverage_id.caption: Fix Coverage ID
fix_coverage_id.description: The normalized identifier for fix coverage, applicable to this vulnerability. Typically useful, when there are multiple affected packages but only a subset have available fixes.

1.caption: Complete
1.description: All affected packages and components have available fixes or patches to remediate the vulnerability.

2.caption: Partial
2.description: Only some of the affected packages and components have available fixes or patches, while others remain vulnerable.

3.caption: None
3.description: No fixes or patches are currently available for any of the affected packages and components.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The fix coverage is not mapped. See the fix_coverage attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

is_exploit_available.caption: Exploit Availability
is_exploit_available.description: Indicates if an exploit or a PoC (proof-of-concept) is available for the reported vulnerability.

is_fix_available.caption: Fix Availability
is_fix_available.description: Indicates if a fix is available for the reported vulnerability.

kb_article_list.caption: Knowledgebase Articles
kb_article_list.description: A list of KB articles or patches related to an endpoint. A KB Article contains metadata that describes the patch or an update.

kb_articles.caption: Knowledgebase Articles
kb_articles.description: The KB article/s related to the entity. A KB Article contains metadata that describes the patch or an update.

last_seen_time.caption: Last Seen
last_seen_time.description: The time when the vulnerability was most recently observed.

packages.caption: Software Packages
packages.description: List of vulnerable packages as identified by the security product

references.caption: References
references.description: A list of reference URLs with additional information about the vulnerability.

related_vulnerabilities.caption: Related Vulnerability IDs
related_vulnerabilities.description: List of vulnerability IDs (e.g. CVE ID) that are related to this vulnerability.

remediation.caption: Remediation Guidance
remediation.description: The remediation recommendations on how to mitigate the identified vulnerability.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The vendor assigned severity of the vulnerability.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A title or a brief phrase summarizing the discovered vulnerability.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor that identified the vulnerability.

vulnerability.caption: Vulnerability Details
vulnerability.description: The vulnerability is an unintended characteristic of a computing component or system configuration that multiplies the risk of an adverse event or a loss occurring either due to accidental exposure, deliberate attack, or conflict with new system components.
vulnerability.name: vulnerability

autonomous_system.caption: Autonomous System
autonomous_system.description: The autonomous system information associated with a domain.

created_time.caption: Registered At
created_time.description: When the domain was registered or WHOIS entry was created.

dnssec_status_id.caption: DNSSEC Status ID
dnssec_status_id.description: Describes the normalized status of DNS Security Extensions (DNSSEC) for a domain.

1.caption: Signed
1.description: The related domain enables the signing of DNS records using DNSSEC.

2.caption: Unsigned
2.description: The related domain does not enable the signing of DNS records using DNSSEC.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The DNSSEC status is not mapped. See the dnssec_status attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The domain name corresponding to the WHOIS record.

email_addr.caption: Registrar Abuse Email Address
email_addr.description: The email address for the registrar's abuse contact

isp.caption: ISP Name
isp.description: The name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP).

isp_org.caption: ISP Org
isp_org.description: The organization name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP). This represents the parent organization or company that owns/operates the ISP. For example, Comcast Corporation would be the ISP org for Xfinity internet service. This attribute helps identify the ultimate provider when ISPs operate under different brand names.

last_seen_time.caption: Last Updated At
last_seen_time.description: When the WHOIS record was last updated or seen at.

name_servers.caption: Name Servers
name_servers.description: A collection of name servers related to a domain registration or other record.

phone_number.caption: Registrar Abuse Phone Number
phone_number.description: The phone number for the registrar's abuse contact

status.caption: Domain Status
status.description: The status of a domain and its ability to be transferred, e.g., clientTransferProhibited.

subdomains.caption: Subdomains
subdomains.description: An array of subdomain strings. Can be used to collect several subdomains such as those from Domain Generation Algorithms (DGAs).

subnet.caption: Subnet Block
subnet.description: The IP address block (CIDR) associated with a domain.

whois.caption: WHOIS
whois.description: The resources of a WHOIS record for a given domain. This can include domain names, IP address blocks, autonomous system information, and/or contact and registration information for a domain.
whois.name: whois

bytestring_t.caption: Byte String
bytestring_t.description: Base 64 encoded immutable byte sequence. Traditional Base 64 is preferred but publishers may use URL-safe Base 64 when known to be acceptable to consumers. These encodings are described in RFC 4648.

datetime_t.caption: Datetime
datetime_t.description:
The Internet Date/Time format as defined in RFC 3339. For example:
2024-09-10T23:20:50.520Z,
2024-09-10 23:20:50.520789Z.

file_hash_t.caption: Hash
file_hash_t.description:
Fingerprint. A value, in any format, that maps an arbitrarily large data item to a much shorter string that uniquely identifies the original data. Examples include cryptographic hashing of a file, code signing, and Network Protocol Fingerprinting (NPF).

Note about name. The type name file_hast_t and the caption "Hash" are used for legacy reasons. This type has been generalized from a file hash to a general fingerprint. The existing type name and caption were retained for backwards compatibility.

file_path_t.caption: File Path
file_path_t.description:
The full path to the file. For example: For example:
c:\windows\system32\svchost.exe.

hostname_t.caption: Hostname
hostname_t.description:
Unique name assigned to a device connected to a computer network. It may be a fully qualified domain name (FQDN). For example:
r2-d2.example.com.,
mx.example.com

ip_t.caption: IP Address
ip_t.description:
Internet Protocol address (IP address), in either IPv4 or IPv6 format. For example:
192.168.200.24,
2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334.

json_t.caption: JSON
json_t.description: Embedded JSON value. A value can be a string, or a number, or true or false or null, or an object or an array. These structures can be nested.

resource_uid_t.caption: Resource UID
resource_uid_t.description: Resource unique identifier. For example, S3 Bucket name or EC2 Instance ID.

subnet_t.caption: Subnet
subnet_t.description:
The subnet represented in a CIDR notation, using the format network_address/prefix_length. The network_address can be in either IPv4 or IPv6 format. The prefix length indicates the number of bits used for the network portion, and the remaining bits are available for host addresses within that subnet. For example:
192.168.1.0/24,
2001:0db8:85a3:0000::/64

timestamp_t.caption: Timestamp
timestamp_t.description:
The timestamp format is the number of milliseconds since the Epoch 01/01/1970 00:00:00 UTC. For example:
1618524549901.
